newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Telebras jumps after telecom rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Telebras jumps after telecom rate hike.

text.p: Brazilian state-owned telecommunications firm Telebras surged in morning trade after the Communications Ministry late Thursday announced a long-awaited rate restructuring, brokers said.
Telebras preferred, the market benchmark, surged 3.91 percent to 119.60 reais, while its common stock gained 3.32 percent to 115.10 reais earlier on the Sao Paulo bourse.
Buy orders of Telebras led the Bovespa index of the 49 most liquid shares to rise 2.61 percent to 9,545 points at 1220 local time/1520 GMT.
Market turnover was a moderate 409.7 million reais ($390.1 million).
The new rates, introduced Friday, will lead to a 3.1 percent net increase in revenues for telecom operators in Brazil.
Among the most important changes, the ministry said residential subscription rates will rise 270.3 percent to 10 reais from 2.70 reais and local pulse rates will rise 61 percent.
Domestic long-distance rates were cut by 32 percent and cuts in international calls varied from 5 percent to 30 percent to the United States, for instance.
The latest rate rebalancing represents the second and final stage of a restructuring of tariffs in the telecom sector before its privatization.
Other telecom stocks also surged earlier. Telesp preferred soared 4.16 percent to 301.11 reais, while Telemig rose 3.4 percent to 152 reais.
Telerj, expected by analysts to benefit most from the rate hike because of its current low profitability, surged 11.99 percent to 169 reais.
